memory_update.text: CYBR should remain a reference anchor for identity, secrets, machine identity, and AI identity controls, but not the main underfollowed alpha lane due to high attention and large-cap status.

TENB is a strong underfollowed/mid-cap candidate for exposure management spanning cloud, AI, identity-adjacent surfaces, OT, and FedRAMP-regulated workloads; verify module-level ARR and Tenable One attach rates.

AVPT is a second-order AI/cloud compliance and data-governance control-plane candidate; evidence is strongest around FedRAMP, ARR growth, Microsoft/Google/Salesforce data governance, and AI-agent governance messaging.

OSPN is a speculative small-cap shadow candidate for high-assurance authentication and regulated digital-workflow security; survival in later layers requires proof that software ARR, NRR, and FIDO/passkey adoption are accelerating.

For this node, scarce or sticky control-plane assets are less about physical supply and more about certifications, integrations, regulated customer trust, identity graph depth, machine/non-human identity coverage, cloud marketplace adoption, and compliance evidence automation.

API-security pure plays and certificate-lifecycle vendors appear limited among US-listed small/mid-cap public companies after consolidation/private ownership; later passes should verify whether exposure is mostly embedded inside larger platforms or recently acquired assets.

summary: Expanded the universe around cloud cybersecurity control-plane software with one reference leader and three underfollowed/smaller discovery candidates. The strongest direct chokepoint exposures found in this pass are identity security for human/machine/AI identities, exposure management spanning IT/cloud/OT/AI, AI-era data governance/compliance automation, and high-assurance authentication for regulated digital transactions. No buy/sell view is implied; this is a research universe expansion only.
